scenarios.title: Replace held options without disturbing the monitor
scenarios.summary: Replace older client-held options and distinguish policy, offers and renewal.
scenarios.objective:
The desk-editor client on 192.0.2.0/24 still holds the old router and DNS options. Finish with a current usable lease on that /24, router 192.0.2.1 and DNS address 203.0.113.53, with at least 40 simulated seconds remaining. Make applied policy serve the same correct parameters to both desk-editor and desk-visitor together in either request order; their assigned addresses may vary.

Preserve the complete desk-office pool and its absent relay setting, and preserve desk-monitor's original server grant and client-held state. Keep that monitor currently configured and the server enabled. Repair policy and obtain current client parameters using the controls; Apply or an acknowledgement alone is not proof that options changed.

scenarios.explanation: Applying policy changes what the server will supply next; it does not rewrite a lease already held by desk-editor. Renewing an eligible lease, or releasing and requesting a new one, obtains the corrected router and DNS options. Check the client-held values and remaining time, then test both new clients together. Preserving the office pool and monitor shows the repair did not disturb the healthy segment. Receiving a DNS address does not itself prove name resolution works.

scenarios.simplifications: Original bounded offline DHCPv4 exercise: one logical server, supplied transport facts, explicit time and no automatic retries/renewal. Native typed fields/actions are not IOS/Linux commands or packet capture. Only DHCP parameters are checked; no routed connectivity, DNS lookup, authentication, snooping or multi-server/failover claim. New-client tests reset separate contexts and do not change current leases. Exclusions/reservations follow the documented local simulator policy. CCNA v1.1 4.3/4.6 slice only, with no full-objective or forthcoming-blueprint credit. Source-only proposal checked2026-10-25; runtime/native acceptance pending.

dhcpv4_teaching.prerequisite_note: After “Reconnect the office client”, distinguish an IPv4 subnet, router and DNS address.

concepts.title: Policy, offers and a client lease
concepts.text: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) supplies a client address, subnet mask and options such as a router and DNS-server addresses. Applied policy describes future offers. Discover asks for an offer; Request accepts that delivered offer. An offer alone does not configure the client. Inspect the client-held lease separately from the server binding.

concepts.title: Apply is not a renewal
concepts.text: Apply changes policy only. A client can still hold its older router and DNS values. A manual Renew can take current policy even before the usual T1 time when the held address remains eligible. If the server cannot extend that address under current policy, it can acknowledge the old grant without changing its options or expiry. Inspect the actual result.

concepts.title: Renew or obtain a new grant
concepts.text: T1 marks the usual scheduled renewal time. Advance changes the explicit simulated clock only; it never sends a request. The worked example waits until T1 and chooses Renew using supplied unicast reachability. A manual earlier Renew is also valid when the address remains eligible. Alternatively Release stops client use, then Discover and Request obtain a new grant. Expiry also ends client use.

concepts.title: Check current work and new requests
concepts.text: Check work inspects current leases and also tests new requests against applied policy in separate reset contexts. These new-client tests do not alter your leases. No particular assigned address is required unless the task names a reservation. Different safe action orders are accepted. Router and DNS options are data here: receiving them does not prove routed connectivity or a working resolver.

Make applied policy serve the same correct parameters to both gallery-desk-editor and gallery-desk-visitor together in either request order; their assigned addresses may vary.

Preserve the complete gallery-desk-office pool and its absent relay setting, and preserve gallery-desk-monitor's original server grant and client-held state. Keep that monitor currently configured and the server enabled. example_actions.explanation: Insert the policy into the draft, inspect the changed pool/relay fields and choose Apply policy. This does not send any client request. Set gallery-desk-scope router to 198.51.100.1, DNS to 198.51.100.53 and lease length to 96 seconds.

scenarios.title: Repair a relay and the selected client subnet
scenarios.summary: Diagnose a remote relay and an answering pool with the wrong subnet.
scenarios.objective:
The annex-branch and annex-visitor clients belong to 10.44.0.0/24 behind the supplied relay interface 10.44.0.1. Diagnose delivery to server 198.18.2.1 and the selected pool. Finish with both clients holding usable /24 leases, router 10.44.0.1, DNS address 203.0.113.53 and at least 40 simulated seconds remaining. Applied policy must support both new clients in either request order.

Exclude 10.44.0.11 in the annex-scope pool. Preserve the complete annex-office pool, that segment's absent relay setting and annex-monitor's original grant/client-held state; finish with the monitor configured and the server enabled. No particular assigned address is required. A delivered offer with a broad mask, or repair of only the relay, is incomplete.

Current leases show what these clients hold; the independent request orders check that the applied policy can serve both newcomers without relying on the current bindings. concepts.title: A relay selects a remote client subnet
concepts.text: A client broadcast does not cross an arbitrary router in this exercise. The supplied relay must be enabled, target this logical DHCP server and identify its client-facing interface. That relay address selects a pool by subnet containment. It is different from the router option sent to clients.

concepts.title: A reply can contain wrong parameters
concepts.text: A broad pool can answer the relay yet supply a mask that is wrong for the physical segment. Inspect the actual held address, mask, router and DNS values. Repair both delivery and the pool; a successful offer or acknowledgement alone is not enough.

concepts.title: Capacity and exclusion
concepts.text: The range is inclusive. An excluded address is unavailable for new grants under this exercise policy; known occupied and infrastructure addresses are also unavailable. Separate new-client tests request in different orders, so a one-client workaround cannot hide insufficient capacity.

concepts.title: Use the actual exchange controls
concepts.text: Edit the selected pool or selected client segment relay, then Apply policy. Discover records a delivered offer. Request uses that current offer. Release and reacquire if a client already holds bad options. Check work tests current clients and new requests; it does not send requests on your behalf.

Preserve the complete gallery-annex-office pool, that segment's absent relay setting and gallery-annex-monitor's original grant/client-held state; finish with the monitor configured and the server enabled. scenarios.title: Hand over a small lease pool safely
scenarios.summary: Retire an old client and provide enough eligible addresses around an exclusion and kiosk reservation.
scenarios.objective:
Retire handover-retired so it no longer holds a client lease. Hand over 172.20.5.0/24 to handover-staff, handover-kiosk, handover-visitor: all three must hold usable leases with router 172.20.5.1, DNS address 203.0.113.53 and at least 40 simulated seconds remaining. In the handover-scope pool, reserve 172.20.5.12 for handover-kiosk and configure that client at the reserved address. Exclude retired address 172.20.5.10 in that pool.

Applied policy must serve all three new clients together in either tested request order. Provide enough eligible addresses for all three clients. Additional valid per-client reservations are allowed; other assigned addresses, range choices and lease lengths may vary.

Preserve the complete handover-office pool and its absent relay setting, plus handover-monitor's original grant and client-held state. Finish with that monitor configured and the server enabled. Retirement by Release or expiry is acceptable; the task does not assert server notification or a working router/DNS service.

concepts.title: Retirement and server ownership
concepts.text: A client lease and the server binding are separate. Release stops the client immediately; the server frees its binding only when the notification can arrive. Otherwise it holds the address until expiry. This task checks that the retired client no longer holds a lease. Release or expiry may achieve that result.

concepts.title: Reserve and exclude deliberately
concepts.text: A reservation supplies an address for a named client. Clients without a reservation use the dynamic range. This exercise excludes addresses from all new grants, including reservations. Reserve the kiosk address and exclude the retired address without excluding the kiosk. Reservations do not automatically configure clients.

concepts.title: Prove a handover, not one lucky allocation
concepts.text: Provide enough eligible addresses for all named clients together. Check work uses independent new-client request orders in addition to current leases. Preserve the explicitly named monitor grant, client-held state and office policy. Other work-pool choices may differ if they meet the task.

concepts.title: Repair a policy without refreshing old evidence
concepts.text: Applying policy does not rewrite existing offers or leases. Stale options, an offer alone and an expired lease cannot pass the current-client checks. Use actual Request, Renew or Release/reacquire where appropriate. Advance never auto-renews. A received router or DNS address remains a parameter, not a tested network service.
